title: You Should...
description: Give and respond to sensible everyday health advice.
objectives: Give and respond to sensible everyday health advice.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to give and respond to sensible everyday health advice. The central language is should/shouldn't for advice. It belongs to the practical context of health & everyday problems. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A2, connect the main message to a time, reason, contrast, or result. Listen for context before choosing the tense or functional phrase. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.english: You should rest and drink water.
blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the you should... exchange.

blocks.english: You shouldn't exercise with a high fever.
blocks.explanation: This you should... model adds a different detail or response.
Use this question or response to keep the you should... exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “You should rest and drink water.” and “You shouldn't exercise with a high fever.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled. Compare the time and viewpoint in each model, and use a linker when two ideas need a clear relationship. Avoid adding advanced forms when the lesson pattern already communicates the message accurately.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: should/shouldn't for advice.

items: Communicative goal: Give and respond to sensible everyday health advice.
Use one clear model, add a relevant detail, and respond to the other speaker.
